requirements.requirement: Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: After wiping stale single-node data directories and restarting etcd with static bootstrap config listing all three peers, etcdctl cluster-health and member list from node1 show all three members (node1, node2, node3) healthy with correct peer/client URLs bound to their static IPs.

requirements.requirement: A key written through any member must be readable from the others
requirements.summary: A key set on node1 was read back correctly on node2 and node3; a key set on node3 was read back correctly on node1, demonstrating bidirectional replication across all three members.

requirements.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was stopped and confirmed inactive; cluster-health from node1 showed node3 unreachable but the cluster still reporting healthy on 2/3 quorum; a new key was successfully written via node1 and read back on both node1 and node2 while node3 remained down. This demonstrates a real bounded disruption and continued read/write availability, not just configuration.

requirements.requirement: Bring the unavailable member back up to date when it returns
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was restarted; cluster-health returned to 3/3 healthy, and node3 itself successfully read both the key written while it was offline and the earlier key, directly demonstrating resynchronization rather than only configuration.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node (independent of public task contract)
requirements.summary: For each of node1, node2, and node3, evidence shows a pre-restart boot_id and healthy cluster baseline, an acknowledged shutdown -r now (connection closed), a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered state (etcd active, cluster 3/3 healthy, member list intact, and prior keys including the outage-period key readable). Boot identities also match the fixed before/after-executor lifecycle snapshots for all three nodes, providing an independent cross-check.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, observed evidence: a 3-member etcd cluster was formed and verified healthy, a key written through any member was confirmed readable from the other two, the cluster demonstrably kept serving reads/writes with node3 stopped (real bounded disruption, not just configuration), and node3 was shown to catch up on the missed key plus return to full health after rejoining. The mandatory provider-wide node-restart protocol was also completed and evidenced for all three nodes, with changed boot identities corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unresolved mutations were found; a couple of failed permission-denied config-write attempts were promptly corrected and left no residue.
limitations: Evidence for the etcd.bak backup file mentioned in an early failed command (cmd-8adf886ffbd648af) was not independently confirmed as absent or present in the lifecycle snapshots, since /etc/default/etcd contents were not captured in before/after-executor snapshots.

Cluster-health and read/write checks during the simulated outage and after node3's return were only queried from node1 and node2; no independent client outside the cluster was used, though this is standard practice and not considered a material gap.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing commands chronologically. apt-get update/install on all three nodes were necessary prerequisites for etcd. Three attempts to append config with a plain heredoc redirect (cmd-8adf886ffbd648af, cmd-0aa229d2d93b48e4, cmd-2cc8bba722b44bb6) failed with 'Permission denied' and produced no state change (config file unmodified per the tail-12 output showing no new lines); the executor immediately corrected course using sudo tee (cmd-5644f4ba7e784f8f, cmd-9adc6962d4824aee, cmd-b38b3bf42c474a74), a legitimate corrective retry, not an unnecessary mutation. Wiping /var/lib/etcd/default on all three nodes (cmd-f6e3cac1ea71456a, cmd-66adbe9e8b0f473b, cmd-32ac5825ee20419c) removed stale single-node auto-bootstrap data that would have blocked correct static 3-member bootstrap; this was bounded, clearly causally tied to achieving the cluster-formation outcome, and not reverted because it was required for the final state. The mandatory sequential reboot of all three nodes was a required action under the node-restart evidence protocol. No unnecessary, broad, destructive, or security-weakening mutations were found; after-executor snapshots show no failed services, no unexpected listening sockets, and only expected boot-tied /tmp entries (systemd-private dirs) differing from before-prepare, consistent with the reboots.
